1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Qingshi for three full days. Lin Xiaoyu closed the apothecary door and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two, and since her father's death she had run the small shop alone.
"Is anyone there?" A man's voice came from outside the door.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated, then opened the door. A young man stood there, soaked through, his left hand pressed to his right arm, blood seeping between his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need this bandaged," Chen Ziming said quietly. "I can pay. Is a hundred and twenty yuan enough?"

She didn't take his money. She just had him sit beside the counter and turned to fetch gauze and medicinal wine. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if cut by a knife. As she cleaned it, she asked how he'd been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent a long time before he said, "I ran into some men on the road. They wanted a letter I was carrying." He took an oil-paper packet from inside his coat and set it on the table. "This letter must reach Baiyun Temple before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun Temple was on the mountain, forty li from Qingshi, and the mountain road was hardest in the rain. She remembered something her father often said: If you save someone, see it through.
"I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow," she said. "Tonight you can sleep in the back room."
2: Before dawn, Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She shouldered a bamboo basket containing dry rations, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm had improved somewhat, but his face was still pale.
When they reached the mountainside, they met the old woodcutter Zhou Dashan. Zhou Dashan recognized Lin Xiaoyu and asked with a smile where she was heading so early.
"To deliver medicine to Baiyun Temple," Lin Xiaoyu replied. She did not mention the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening, three outsiders were asking about an injured young man at the town entrance. Be careful."

Chen Ziming's face grew even paler. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man and led Chen Ziming off the main road onto a narrow trail known only to herb gatherers. The path was narrow and slippery; she walked ahead, each step planted firmly.

By noon the rain had finally stopped. The mountain mist slowly lifted, revealing the roof of Baiyun Temple in the distance. A nun stood at the temple gate; her name was Zhao Qiuyue, and she served as the temple's receptionist.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper packet, looked at the red seal on the closure, and nodded. "Master has been waiting for this letter for 2 years," she said. "You've had a hard journey."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled and said, "Then next time you come to Qingshi, help me fix the roof of the medicine shop."
